messages.content:
You are proposing scientific conjectures. A conjecture is a bold, specific,
falsifiable claim or approach -- not a summary, not a plan, and not a hedge.
Write plainly.

What is the best technique for turning an abstract specification into executable code — such that the result actually holds its commitments?

Stay within this direction: compilation by denotational semantics preserving step-indexed logical relations

Generate 10 candidate conjectures within that direction, sampled from the
full distribution of responses you could give. For each, give the
conjecture and your estimated probability that it is the response you would
give to this prompt. Every candidate's probability must be below 0.10.
Output exactly one JSON object and nothing else:
{"candidates": [{"conjecture": "<2-4 sentences>", "probability": <number below 0.10>}, ... 10 items]}

message.content: {"candidates": [{"conjecture": "The reliability of compiled code preserving its abstract specification correlates with the density of step-index points aligned to the source language's reduction semantics, not merely the depth of the logical relation. Specifically, compilers that instrument step-indexed logical relations at every beta-reduction equivalence class, rather than at every machine step, achieve a 3x lower specification-violation rate in generated code.", "probability": 0.087}, {"conjecture": "Denotational-semantic compilation into continuation-passing style with a step-indexed logical relation over continuations yields executable code that is observationally equivalent to the abstract specification under any adversarial context, provided the specification is expressible in a dependent type theory of at strength CIC.", "probability": 0.079}, {"conjecture": "The minimum number of step-indexed logical relation layers required to fully preserve an abstract specification through compilation is exactly the stratification depth of the specification's fixpoint operators plus one. Any fewer layers admits a semantic gap exploitable by a non-terminating adversarial context.", "probability": 0.065}, {"conjecture": "For any abstract specification written in a monadic effect calculus, compilation by denotational semantics into a target language with effect handlers preserves all specification commitments if and only if the step-indexed logical relation is defined over the residual effect monad rather than the source effect monad.", "probability": 0.071}, {"conjecture": "Step-indexed logical relations over denotational semantics can be made computationally decidable for verification purposes by restricting the abstract specification to a fragment of intuitionistic linear logic, yielding an automated compiler that produces certified executable code with complexity O(n^3) in specification size.", "probability": 0.058}, {"conjecture": "Compiling abstract specifications via a denotational semantics into an intermediate representation tagged with step-index semantics is dominated by a single recursive scheme.", "probability": 0.062}, {"conjecture": "The step-indexed logical relations approach to compilation fails to preserve abstract specification cardinality of the nondeterministic choice set rather than computation steps.", "probability": 0.068}, {"conjecture": "A compiler based on denotational semantics with step-indexed logical relations
